svg.text: On imaging platforms a cell is not measured — it is drawn. The line decides what the cell expresses.
molecules at coordinates + a nuclear stain
dashed = true membranes, not in the data
the cell boundary has to be inferred
segmentation assigns each dot to a cell
Tumour cells lose their outer cytoplasm
The thin cell's outline reaches into
counts in the thin cell, true vs segmented
Neither: it is where the line was
drawn. Check it on the image
⚠️ The imaging version of “a spot is not a cell”: thin, squeezed cells (macrophages, T cells, fibroblasts) are hit hardest.
💡 Membrane stains and transcript-aware tools (Baysor) help. Visium HD bins → cells (bin2cell) faces the same problem.
